items.prompt: In a document processing system, a processing coordinator must submit an extraction job. a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects The design review focuses on synchronous versus asynchronous request boundaries. The normal path is healthy and the design must show where the decision belongs. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is keep only deadline-critical work synchronous and make the asynchronous handoff durable and observable..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Keep only deadline-critical work synchronous and make the asynchronous handoff durable and observable. In this normal path for document processing, the boundary changes coupling, retry ownership, user feedback, and recovery semantics. The owner must also make a worker retry after an unknown result observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide synchronous versus asynchronous request boundaries independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a worker retry after an unknown result as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Keep only deadline-critical work synchronous and make the asynchronous handoff durable and observable. It addresses a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects through an explicit mechanism and keeps a worker retry after an unknown result inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The boundary changes coupling, retry ownership, user feedback, and recovery semantics. The applicability case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For document processing, the decision keeps a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a worker retry after an unknown result as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Synchronous versus asynchronous request boundaries” to terminology recall. Distinguish protocol mechanics from domain boundaries; a fashionable API style is not automatically the correct contract. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce synchronous versus asynchronous request boundaries must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
